walkthroughs.body_html:
Rural Environments — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Rural Environments brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Rural Environments.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which African region suffers severe desertification?
options: Sahel
Maghreb
Cape
Horn of Africa

mcqs.q: What is the maximum rainfall in hot deserts?
options: 100mm
250mm
500mm

mcqs.q: Why do people move from rural to urban areas in LICs?
options: Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
Because cities in poor countries are always better than the countryside.
A combination of push factors (rural poverty, lack of services, agricultural change) and pull factors (perceived jobs, education, healthcare) — though reality often disappoints.

mcqs.q: Why do glaciated valleys have a U-shape rather than a V-shape?
options: Because the government forces them to move to cities.
Glaciers occupy the whole valley width, eroding the sides as well as the floor, producing steep sides and a flat floor (U-shape); rivers erode mainly downwards, leaving V-shape.
Glaciers cut U-shapes because ice is shaped like a U.
Glaciers carve V-shaped valleys just like rivers do.

mcqs.q: What happens in Stage 2 of the Demographic Transition Model?
options: Glaciers carve V-shaped valleys just like rivers do.
Death rates fall rapidly (due to better food, sanitation and medicine) while birth rates remain high, causing rapid population growth.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
Birth rates rise rapidly because people want larger families.
